hints: Because P is on the point of sliding down the plane, limiting friction acts up the plane and satisfies $F=\mu R$.
Resolve perpendicular to the plane: the horizontal $12\,\mathrm N$ force presses into it, so $R=6g\cos\theta+12\sin\theta$.
Resolve parallel to the plane in equilibrium: $F=6g\sin\theta-12\cos\theta$.
Substitute these expressions into $F=\mu R$, use $g=10$, and divide numerator and denominator by $\cos\theta$.
Simplify to the required expression in $\tan\theta$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: Resolve forces acting on the particle of mass $6\text{ kg}$ perpendicular to the inclined plane:
The horizontal force of $12\text{ N}$ acts into the plane with perpendicular component $12\sin\theta$, and gravity has perpendicular component $6g\cos\theta$:
$$R = 6g\cos\theta + 12\sin\theta = 60\cos\theta + 12\sin\theta$$

Step 2: Resolve forces parallel to the inclined plane in limiting equilibrium:
Impending motion is down the slope, so the limiting friction $F$ acts up the incline alongside the parallel component of the horizontal force $12\cos\theta$, balancing the component of weight down the plane $6g\sin\theta$:
$$F + 12\cos\theta = 6g\sin\theta$$
$$F = 60\sin\theta - 12\cos\theta$$

Step 3: Apply the limiting friction law $F = \mu R$:
$$\mu = \frac{F}{R} = \frac{60\sin\theta - 12\cos\theta}{60\cos\theta + 12\sin\theta}$$

Step 4: Divide every term in the numerator and denominator by $12\cos\theta$:
$$\mu = \frac{\frac{60\sin\theta}{12\cos\theta} - \frac{12\cos\theta}{12\cos\theta}}{\frac{60\cos\theta}{12\cos\theta} + \frac{12\sin\theta}{12\cos\theta}} = \frac{5\tan\theta - 1}{5 + \tan\theta}$$
Thus, $\mu = \frac{5\tan\theta - 1}{5 + \tan\theta}$ as required.

hints: Use the coefficient expression from part (a) and the physical requirement $\mu>0$.
For acute $\theta$, the denominator $5+\tan\theta$ is positive, so require the numerator $5\tan\theta-1$ to be positive.
Solve $\tan\theta>1/5$ and intersect it with the given acute-angle range $0^\circ<\theta<90^\circ$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: State the physical constraint on the coefficient of friction $\mu$:
The coefficient of friction must be strictly positive ($\mu > 0$):
$$\frac{5\tan\theta - 1}{5 + \tan\theta} > 0$$

Step 2: Analyze the denominator for acute angles ($0^\circ < \theta < 90^\circ$):
Since $\tan\theta > 0$ for acute angles, $5 + \tan\theta > 5 > 0$, meaning the denominator is always positive.

Step 3: Solve for the numerator being positive:
$$5\tan\theta - 1 > 0 \implies 5\tan\theta > 1 \implies \tan\theta > \frac{1}{5} = 0.2$$
$$\theta > \arctan(0.2) \approx 11.3099^\circ \approx 11.3^\circ$$

Step 4: State the complete solution interval for acute angles:
$$11.3^\circ < \theta < 90^\circ$$
The set of possible values of $\theta$ is $11.3^\circ < \theta < 90^\circ$.
